reason: The narrative demonstrates that strict, inflexible hierarchical authority is problematic and should be circumvented when it conflicts with justice. Saul's harsh, rigid application of his oath—condemning his own son Jonathan to death merely for unknowingly tasting honey, despite Jonathan's heroic military victory—is presented as unjust. The people's righteous defiance of Saul's strict command, ransoming Jonathan to save his life (וַיִּפְדּוּ הָעָם אֶת־ יוֹנָתָן וְלֹא־ מֵֽת), is portrayed as morally correct and aligned with God's will. Their statement (הֲ‍ֽיוֹנָתָן׀ יָמוּת֙ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה הַיְשׁוּעָה הַגְּדוֹלָה) emphasizes that merit and accomplishment should override strict hierarchical rules. The text thus discourages blind adherence to rigid authority when it contradicts justice and recognition of genuine achievement.
